tours.name: 42 Traverse - One Way Shuttle
tours.description:
Arrive at Owhango Adventures Base where there is safe and secure parking for your vehicle while you cycle the famous 42 Traverse.

Intermediate: Grade 3

The 42 Traverse is a challenging track best suited to experienced, well-equipped people. It leads through fantastic native forest and the awesome Canyon valley. There are superb views back to the volcanoes of Tongariro National Park.

The route is an old logging road that gets its name from the original 'State Forest 42'. It is popular for a range of activities: mountain biking, quad and trail biking, four-wheel driving (summer only), horse riding, fishing, hunting and hiking.

The area is remote and there are often slips, fallen trees and other damage on the track. Sections of the track are very technical. Read the Know Before You Go section carefully for information on what to pack and expect.

The 42 Traverse route: from Kapoors Road to Ohinetonga Road
The track can be used in either direction. However, it is easier for bikers to go from Kapoors Road to Ohinetonga Road, as there is more downhill that way.

tours.name: Mount Maunganui Scenic Flight
tours.location: New Zealand/Bay of Plenty Region/Mount Maunganui
tours.description:
Take to the skies for a flight around one of New Zealand’s most iconic coastal landmarks: Mount Maunganui. Lifting off from the coast, you’ll soon be soaring above golden beaches, turquoise waters, and the rugged green slopes of Mauao, the sacred mountain that anchors the Bay of Plenty.

From the air, discover Pilot Bay and Main Beach, two beaches consistently ranked among the best in the country. In the distance the views stretch to the world famous Coromandel, Mt Ruapehu and White Island.

This short but spectacular flight offers a unique window into the natural beauty and local life of the Bay, perfect for visitors or locals seeing it all anew from above.

tours.name: Coromandel Scenic Flight
tours.location: New Zealand/Bay of Plenty Region/Mount Maunganui
tours.description:
Take off from Tauranga and discover the Coromandel from above on this scenic flight. Soar over golden beaches, lush forests, and coastal highlights like Cathedral Cove and Hot Water Beach.

See one of New Zealand’s most beautiful regions from the air on this scenic flight from Tauranga to the Coromandel Peninsula. Perfect for visitors wanting to explore more of the country’s natural beauty in a short time, this experience offers coastal views and a unique aerial perspective on iconic landmarks such as the world-famous Cathedral Cove set of the Chronicles of Narnia.

Departing from Tauranga, you’ll fly over the sparkling waters of the Bay of Plenty, with incredible views of Mount Maunganui, Matakana Island, and the surrounding coastline. As you head north, the landscape opens up to reveal the rugged terrain of the Coromandel—famous for its secluded beaches, forested hills, and crystal-clear bays.

tours.name: ICONIC KARITANE MAORI TOUR & MOERAKI BOULDERS
tours.description:
*A full-day tour transporting you along the North Otago coastline to the beautiful beach side town of Karitane. Steeped in Maori and early European history, local Maori of the area have established a cultural walking tour to the Huriawa Peninsula to showcase their historic Pā site (fortified village or stronghold) known as Te Pā a Te Wera. Your local guide will tell you about legendary Maori warriors, of fierce battles and rivalries of days gone by, while taking in the views from this remarkable coastal headland.

Also included is a visit the famous Moeraki Boulders on Koekohe Beach nearby. These giant rocks situated right on the ocean shore are indeed a geological marvel, as well as having strong cultural significance for Maori. They formed millions of years ago into perfectly round spheres and have been uncovered by the breaking waves and eroding sand.

The tour will visit Dunedin City for a brief look at some of the sightseeing highlights, such as Baldwin Street (World's Steepest Street), Dunedin Railway Station and the Octagon (city center) before heading back to Port.

Enjoy a scenic journey from Port Chalmers as you explore the vibrant city of Dunedin and the Otago Peninsula – known as the wildlife capital of New Zealand.

Begin with a stop at one of the most photographed buildings in the Southern Hemisphere – the iconic Dunedin Railway Station. Then, get your camera ready as we wind our way along the Otago Peninsula, taking in views of the harbour, bays, beaches, and an array of wading birds.

The highlight of your experience is a 1.5-hour guided tour at Penguin Place, a private conservation reserve dedicated to protecting the endangered Yellow-Eyed Penguin. During the tour, you may have the chance to see these rare penguins, along with other native wildlife such as New Zealand fur seals, sea lions, and occasionally little blue penguins in their nesting sites.

tours.name: The Cultural River Expedition
tours.description:
🌊✨ Experience the Spirit of the Whanganui Awa (River) on a 3-Day Guided River Journey with Owhango Adventures! ✨🌊

Imagine gliding down the majestic Whanganui River, surrounded by landscapes and the rich tapestry of Māori culture. Join us for an 3-Day, 2-Night Guided and Catered River Journey, where you will be led by local Kaitiaki (guides), the guardians of the land and river, who are tangata whenua (people of the land).

In a traditional 6-person waka (canoe) or traditional 2-person Canadian style canoe, you will not only experience the serenity of the river but also connect deeply with the stories, traditions, and wisdom of the Māori people. Each paddle stroke will take you through lush native bush, past cliffs, and into the heart of a culture that has thrived for centuries.

🍃 What to Expect:

Culturally Enriching Experiences: Engage with local customs and stories that bring the landscape to life.
Scenery: Discover the natural beauty of Aotearoa, from tranquil waters to lush riverbanks.
Community Connection: Bu
highlights: Free night accommodation at our Base in Owhango the night prior to your journey departure.
Rapid Water Flow: The Whanganui River features various sections with different water flow speeds. Sudden changes in flow can present challenges, especially for novice paddlers.
Obstacles: The river is home to natural obstacles such as fallen trees, rocks, and shallow areas. Navigating these hazards requires skill and awareness.
Weather Conditions: Weather can change rapidly in this region. Rain can lead to increased river flows and potential flooding. Always check the forecast before heading out.
Wildlife Encounters: While the river is home to beautiful wildlife, encounters with animals can pose risks. Be cautious and respectful of their habitats.
Hypothermia: Even in warmer months, the temperature of the water can be quite cold. Proper gear is essential to mitigate the risk of hypothermia.
Fatigue: Paddling can be physically demanding, especially on longer trips. It’s important to pace yourself and take regular breaks to avoid exhaustion.
Navigation Skills: Understanding how to read river maps and navigation skills are crucial. Being lost or disoriented can lead to dangerous situations.

tours.name: Twilight at The OPERA
tours.description:
Our Twilight at The OPERA tour provides a unique opportunity to experience our private eco-reserve at sunset.

This tour offers a unique opportunity to view our

, hoiho (yellow-eyed penguins) and a variety of our marine and coastal species, in their natural habitat.

This 90-minute guided tour consists of three parts.

Begin your experience in a theatre setting, where you will learn about our conservation work and the hoiho (yellow-eyed penguin) and efforts to protect them.

Then move into our rehabilitation centre where hoiho (yellow-eyed penguins) and other penguin species can be seen up close (when birds are in our care).

Finally, a short bus trip into our reserve where you are guided on an approximately 2km (1.25 mile) nature walk with the potential to see numerous plants and animals, including yellow-eyed penguins and little penguins, fur seals, sea lions, and several species of shore and land birds, all of which reside in the reserve.

穿越山脉之后，您的第一站美食之旅将在一家手工芝士作坊展开。在这里，您将看到和品尝由新西兰专业奶酪师傅手工制作的各式精美奶酪产品。

参观马丁堡三家顶级精品酒庄，带您了解该地区的葡萄酒知识，品尝精选葡萄酒，领略其独特风味。酒庄的选择不固定，受季节和时段的影响。酒庄午餐可根据游客要求提供，游客自费。

返程

行程最后，您将通过雷穆塔卡山脉返回惠灵顿市中心。

驱车穿越壮丽的雷穆塔卡山脉，一路进入美食与美酒并存的怀拉拉帕地区。
在手工芝士作坊品尝新西兰手工奶酪，了解当地乳制品匠艺。

start time may change to suit the arrival time of your cruise ship

Highlights

**This tour includes specialist guided tours at both Albatross and Penguin colonies **

Start promptly at 9:00 am from the ship's wharf at Port Chalmers (if your ship is scheduled for a later arrival we can customize the tour to suit). Travel along the harbour road to Dunedin City and head to the Otago Peninsula, home to the rare Yellow Eyed Penguins and majestic Royal Albatross. Experience the pristine views from up high along the top road of the Otago Peninsula. See plenty of sheep on the small farms and learn about the local Maori who have lived in Dunedin and on the Otago Peninsula for centuries. We arrive at Penguin Place for the first wildlife tour of the day at the Yellow Eyed Penguin Conservation Reserve. After the tour we have time for a light lunch before heading to Taiaroa Heads at the end of the Peninsula for the second wildlife tour at the Royal Albatross Colony. After completing both wildlife tours on the Otago Peninsula, we head back to Dunedin City for a brief city sights tour which includes a visit to Baldwin Street on route to the ship's wharf at Port Chalmers.

tours.name: One-hour Wildlife Cruise
tours.description:
Sit back and enjoy the scenery as our sturdy boat explores the stunningly beautiful and rugged coastline near the entrance of the Otago Harbour. Our crew will give you a full commentary during your cruise about our local wildlife, history and geology.

The trip will travel past the beautiful Aramoana Beach and it’s tidal sandflats. We often spot sea lions here, sprawled out, basking in the sun. These impressive animals can weigh almost half a tonne. After nearly being wiped out by early settlers they have recently started returning to the sandy beaches around the southern coastline of New Zealand. The sealion population is now growing steadily.

Across the other side of the harbour channel you’ll see remnants of the areas military history. Several lookout posts and gun emplacements were built in to the rocky hill, connected by tunnels. They are now a popular spot for local fisherman.

You’ll see uninterrupted views of the world's only mainland colony of royal albatross. We want to get you c

tours.description:
Come riding with us!
About

Enjoy a guided bike tour along the beautiful Karāpiro section of the Waikato River Trails.

Our guides let you know what's coming up, and share their knowledge and history of the area as you soak in the surroundings of extremely popular section of trail, which takes your through wetland to Arapuni Village.

The Waikato River Trails offer great views and spectacular flora and fauna only found in New Zealand.

Boasting more than 100km of Grade 2 and 3 riding (easy to intermediate), there is a trail for everyone- and we can take you on guided tour along the Karāpiro section.

Starting at Arapuni Dam (best for beginners) or Jones Landing (for more intermediate riders), our guides will let you know what's coming up, and share their local knowledge and history of the area.

Meet at Riverside Adventures base on Horahora Road and hop on board a shuttle. You can use your own bike or hire one of ours - we have mountain bikes and e-bikes.

About

Our guides let you know what's coming up, and share their knowledge and history of the area as you soak in the surroundings of extremely popular section of trail, which takes you from through the town of Town of Trees and Champions out to the famous Lake Karapiro.

Its unique concrete surface (the longest concrete trail in the country in fact!) and at three metres wide is accessible to a huge range of users and abilities!

You will enjoy an easy hour-long walk along the Waikato River trail where you will experience views of nearby Lake Arapuni and beyond.

We will meet you at the end of the trail with your bikes. The 2km ride begins at the Arapuni Dam and continues along the Waikato River Trail to village of Arapuni where you will stop for lunch at the popular Rhubarb Cafe.

Following lunch, your bike ride continues for 12km, returning you back to our base where you can pause before the day’s final adventure.

Next, your guide will help you get kitted out and ready for the Twilight Kayak Glow Worm Tour.

Over the next three hours bask in the magic of the Pokaiwhenua canyon as you hear stories from your experienced guide, a few tasty treats and, finally, an experience like no other as you float silently back through the canyon surrounded by twinkling glow worms, stars above

On this private tour, you will visit three of Waiheke’s top vineyards and sample a range of their wines. Along the way enjoy a commentated scenic drive, learning about the Island’s history, geography, people and culture from your knowledgeable local guide.

After your wine tasting experience sit back, relax and enjoy lunch at one of our world class vineyards. Included is a two course lunch including glass of wine.

After lunch your guide will return you to the ferry or Island accommodation. If you would prefer to swap a vineyard for an olive oil mill, gin or whisky tasting, craft brewery tasting or guided walk just let us know. We are happy to tailor the tour to suit you!

tours.name: Half Day Scenic Wine and Lunch
tours.description:
The tour commences with a drive along the scenic northern route, taking in spectacular views of the Hauraki Gulf and beyond to the Coromandel Peninsula.

Visit three vineyards for wine tasting with a delicious vineyard platter-style lunch at the second vineyard, including a glass of wine.

If time allows, after lunch head towards Onetangi, a 1.87-kilometre long, north-facing beach with beautiful old Pohutukawa trees on the foreshore. For many years it has been the site of the Onetangi Beach Races.

The final stop is at a picturesque vineyard overlooking the Hauraki Gulf. Enjoy a wine tasting here and take in the view.

If you wish, from here you can stay on for dinner (at your own expense) and make your own way back to the ferry when you are ready or alternatively the guide will return you to the Waiheke Wharf in time to catch the 5pm ferry back to Auckland.

Guests need to call 24 hours prior to their tour to confirm their pick up address.

About

Embark on a journey through the landscapes of Fox Glacier. A gentle, gradual climb making this adventure accessible to all ages and fitness levels.

Departing at the Glacier Valley Eco Tours base in the township of Franz Josef Glacier - we’ll drive you to Fox Glacier from Franz Josef Glacier (a 30-minute drive) or if you are staying in Fox Glacier we'll pick you up from our meeting point in the Fox Glacier township (or your accommodation).

​This scenic trail meanders through the lush, historic glaciated rainforest of Westland Tai Poutini National Park, where you'll encounter magnificent rata and rimu trees, vibrant mosses, and views of the upper Fox Glacier, the Fox Neve and Mt Tasman—one of New Zealand's tallest peaks. Along the way, our knowledgeable guides will share fascinating insights into the area's geology, glaciation, and thermology (including a chance to dip your hand in a geothermal spring) and its diverse flora and fauna.

​

Departing at the Glacier Valley Eco Tours base in the township of Franz Josef Glacier - we’ll drive you to Fox Glacier from Franz Josef Glacier (a 30-minute drive) or if you are staying in Fox Glacier we'll pick you up from our meeting point in the Fox Glacier township (or your accommodation).

About

Embark on the Ōkārito Nature Tour with Glacier Valley Eco Tours and explore an of New Zealand's South Westland.

Just a 20-minute drive from Franz Josef Glacier, the small coastal village of Ōkārito offers an unparalleled bird-watching experience amidst natural diversity. Suitable for all ages and abilities, this tour includes a shuttle service from the Franz Josef township or guests can meet us in Okarito. The tour guides you through lush rainforests, estuaries, sea cliffs and wetlands, revealing views of the Southern Alps, including Aoraki/Mt Cook, Mt Tasman and even Franz Josef Glacier on clear days. Delve into the rich history of gold mining and early settlement with the opportunity to encounter the area's rich birdlife - up to 76 bird species, such as the famous white heron (Kotuku), fern birds, kakariki and kea.

Visit the Ōkārito Community Native Plant Nursery to plant a native tree as part of our Okarito Restoration project. 雷穆塔卡山脉观光路线

从惠灵顿出发穿越连绵起伏的雷穆塔卡山脉，前往著名的怀拉拉帕地区，该地区以其世界级的美食生产商而闻名。途中会在海拔555米的雷穆塔卡山顶停留，欣赏令人叹为观止的360度美景。

手工芝士作坊

穿越山脉之后，您的第一站美食之旅将在一家手工芝士作坊展开。在这里，您将看到和品尝由新西兰专业奶酪师傅手工制作的各式精美奶酪产品。

精品酒庄品酒

下一站，您将前往世界级的马丁堡葡萄酒产区，该地区以黑皮诺葡萄酒闻名，您将在当地一家顶级酒庄品尝一系列精选葡萄酒，并享用精致的手工奶酪拼盘。如有需要，还可应要求安排额外的自费午餐。

tours.name: 惠灵顿特色景点半日游中文团
tours.description:
惠灵顿特色景点精品团半日游行程为3个小时。精品小团（2-11人），私人专车为旅行提供私密空间。资深的中文导游提供惠灵顿各个景点的详细解说。行程囊括了众多惠灵顿知名景点：从惠灵顿维多利亚山，东方湾，维塔工作室，惠灵顿缆车，植物园，布鲁克林风力发电站，国会大厦等。

What's included

专业的司机和中文导游提供路线和景点的解说

全程专车服务

我们一般使用奔驰12座的豪华旅游车。如小团的话可能会选择不同车辆

What's not included

惠灵顿缆车票（单程$6.5NZD/位，游客可以自行选择乘坐至植物园山顶，不坐缆车的游客可跟随专车去植物园山顶）

国会大厦内部的跟团游门票。（友情提醒：国会大厦内部的跟团游时间不固定，需提前几个月预订，否则不能确保有余票。）

Itinerary
维多利亚山顶观景台

从惠灵顿海滨出发，驱车上维多利亚山，到达维多利亚山顶观景台，欣赏惠灵顿市及其风景如画的海港的壮丽360度全景。

东方湾

沿着东方湾和埃文斯湾的海岸线驱车，可观赏到各种悬挂在山坡上的私人住宅使用的小缆车。

维塔工作室

简短地停留在标志性的“Wellington Blown Away”标志处，然后参观著名的维塔工商店，这是位于Miramar的维塔工作室旅游的中心。这不仅是一个零售店，它还是一个充满创意的电影人物和道具特效工作室。在维塔，您可以与等身雕像自拍，漫步于迷你博物馆，并观看独家纪录片。这里是电影爱好者的天堂。

布鲁克林风力发电站

布鲁克林风力发电机是惠灵顿标志性的山顶地标，也是新西兰首个具有商业可行性的风力发电机。

惠灵顿缆车及玫瑰园

返回市中心，短暂停留旧银行拱廊的周总拍照打卡点。可在附近选择乘坐著名的惠灵顿缆车至植物园山顶浏览市貌（票价自理），亦可漫步于诺伍德夫人玫瑰园和温室中心浏览拍照。

国会大厦、总统府建筑

参观国会大厦、总统府等建筑（不含国会大厦内部的跟团游）。

Highlights
登上维多利亚观景台，俯瞰惠灵顿港及城市全景，感受“风城”之名不是浪得虚名。
驱车沿 东方湾 及 Miramar半岛海岸线，体验惠灵顿独特的海岸风光与自然气息。

tours.description:
Immerse yourself in the ultimate blend of adventure and cultural discovery with this extraordinary full-day combo! Begin your journey with a fully guided exploration of Mt. Tarawera, a site of immense geological and cultural significance. Infamous for its catastrophic eruption in 1886, Mt. Tarawera offers volcanic landscapes and unmatched 360° panoramic views. As you trek through this dramatic terrain, your guide will share fascinating insights into the eruption’s impact on the region, including the creation of the world’s youngest geothermal valley, Waimangu. Suitable for all ages, this tour also includes the option to run into the heart of the volcanic crater for an extra adrenaline rush.

After your volcanic adventure, the cultural experience continues at Te Puia, New Zealand’s premier Māori cultural and geothermal attraction. Join the Te Pō Guided Tour, where you’ll witness the world-famous Pohutu Geyser and explore geothermal wonder

tours.name: Castle to Cruise Tour
tours.description:
Take a wonderful journey back in time, on a guided tour of New Zealand's castle.

Built in 1871, it took two hundred workers roughly three years to build the exterior shell and a further twelve years for master European craftsmen to finish the interior. Over the years the castle and grounds fell in to ruin and disrepair. In 1967 the property was bought by the Barker family who have spent many years restoring it to its former grandeur. The rooms are once again filled with original artworks, clothing and furniture.

During the tour you’ll see the magnificent carved ceilings, antiques and painstakingly restored original features. Hear the scandalous and tragic history of the original owner, William Larnach who took his own life with a single shot to the head. Climb the spiral staircase to the rooftop tower for 360° views of the Otago Peninsula. We highly recommend a short walk around the beautiful gardens, recognized to be of international significance.

Time is allowed to explore the grounds or take tea in the Ballroom Cafe. You’ll then meet your guide

tours.description:
Enjoy everything the Castle to Cruise Tour offers and include an opportunity to spot the world's rarest penguin in the wild!

Bus across the Otago Peninsula and explore the grand Larnach Castle. Let our guide tell you the scandalous story of original owner William Larnach. Explore the building with its fabulous craftsmanship art and antiques. Walk the carefully curated gardens and take tea in the Ballroom Café.

Next, you'll join our Wildlife Cruise, with it's uninterrupted views of the world’s only mainland nesting place of royal albatross. Watch as these huge birds glide in from the ocean and soar high above their hillside nest sites.

Your skipper will guide the boat close to the base of dramatic volcanic cliffs, with a historic lighthouse perched high above. Beneath the cliffs you’ll see fur seals play on rocky outcrops and swim in tidal pools.

A short cruise out at sea and you’ll spot rarely seen ocean birds including other albatross species, cormorants and petrels. We sometimes spot sea lions, blue penguins, dolphins and other marine mammals.

tours.name: Peninsula Encounters + Albatross Tour
tours.description:
This is our premium land-based wildlife experience.

A small-group bus tour from Dunedin. Join a local guide for an exploration of the Otago Peninsula.

Travel over the high road with postcard views of the harbour and coast. You’ll travel past quaint communities and rural farms. Spot wading birds as your mini-bus explores around the inlets and the wetland eco-systems.

Your tour will visit a remote Otago Peninsula beach. A short walk from the mini-bus will provide dramatic views of rugged coastal cliffs, offshore islands and perhaps some huge sea lions.

Watch as these majestic birds glide past on three metre wingspans, or as they feed their chicks at the nest.

tours.description:
Karioi Canyoning takes you into an ancient volcanic landscape beneath Mt Karioi, following a lava-formed creek through lush native bush. Wearing warm canyoning wetsuits, you will scramble, climb and abseil waterfalls and traverse volcanic boulders while listening to your guide’s geological, ecological and cultural stories. Suited to those with moderate fitness and a sense of adventure, the experience blends thrilling movement through water and rock with the sights and sounds of native birds and flowing streams.

tours.name: 惠灵顿城市Eco徒步之旅
tours.description:
行程从宏伟的新古典主义火车站出发，步行前往国会大厦，了解新西兰的政治文化；随后沿着惠灵顿的地震断层线前往植物园，在原生与外来植物交织的景观中，认识新西兰独特的自然生态。到达植物园顶端的缆车观景台后，我们将饱览城市美景、辨识地标，并了解惠灵顿的地形布局。随后乘坐缆车（含缆车单程票）到达繁华Lambton Quay街道并前往热闹的古巴街（Cuba Street）稍作休憩。行程最终在滨海区的国家博物馆结束。

What's included

含惠灵顿缆车单程车票

专业的司机和中文导游提供路线和景点的解说

Itinerary

惠灵顿火车站（Wellington Railway Station）
在火车站正门集合，导游欢迎并介绍行程。随后穿过气势恢宏的新古典主义建筑大厅，经地下通道前往国会大厦附近。
⏱ 约 15 分钟

新西兰蜂巢、国会大厦、议会图书馆建筑
在这里将介绍新西兰的政治体系与文化，以及惠灵顿作为首都所扮演的角色。同时讲解周边建筑的风格特色及其功能。
⏱ 约 15 分钟

惠灵顿植物园（Wellington Botanic Garden）
漫步于郁郁葱葱的花园、公共绿地与原生丛林之中，外来植物与本土动植物在此和谐共存。导游将讲解惠灵顿独特的生物多样性与自然环境。
⏱ 约 30 分钟

惠灵顿缆车站（Wellington Cable Car）
穿过植物园，抵达历史悠久的缆车顶站。这里视野开阔，可俯瞰城市景观，是了解惠灵顿整体布局、拍照留念的绝佳地点。并乘坐缆车到达商业中心。
⏱ 约 15 分钟

⏱ 约 15 分钟

新西兰蜂巢、国会大厦、议会图书馆建筑
在这里将介绍新西兰的政治体系与文化，以及惠灵顿作为首都所扮演的角色。同时讲解周边建筑的风格特色及其功能。
⏱ 约 15 分钟

惠灵顿植物园（Wellington Botanic Garden）
漫步于郁郁葱葱的花园、公共绿地与原生丛林之中，外来植物与本土动植物在此和谐共存。导游将讲解惠灵顿独特的生物多样性与自然环境。
⏱ 约 30 分钟

惠灵顿缆车站（Wellington Cable Car）
穿过植物园，抵达历史悠久的缆车顶站。这里视野开阔，可俯瞰城市景观，是了解惠灵顿整体布局、拍照留念的绝佳地点。并乘坐缆车到达商业中心。
⏱ 约 15 分钟

穿越Lambton Quay街道和古巴街（Cuba Street）
穿行于惠灵顿繁华商业街道的Lambton Quay，途径旧拱廊银行(old bank arcade) ——明星取景打卡处。最终抵达城市活力中心——古巴街（Cuba Street）。
⏱ 约 1小时

新西兰国家博物馆（Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa）
随后沿着迷人的海滨步行，行程在新西兰国家博物馆 Te Papa Tongarewa 结束。
⏱ 约 1小时

tours.name: Mt Tarawera Hike & Wai Ariki Restorative Bathing Experience
tours.description:
Discover the extraordinary beauty of Mt Tarawera on a fully guided premium walking experience. Journey across this sacred volcanic landscape as your expert guide shares the powerful history, cultural significance, and stories of the 1886 eruption that shaped the region. Take in 360° views from the summit of Ruawāhia and experience the thrill of descending into the heart of the volcanic crater, a truly unique experience found nowhere else in New Zealand.

After your adventure, transition from exploration to restoration at Wai Ariki Hot Springs & Spa, Rotorua’s premier cultural wellness sanctuary. Enjoy an one-hour restorative bathing experience inspired by traditional Māori healing practices, featuring geothermal mineral pools, herbal infusions, hydrotherapy, and a revitalising cold plunge overlooking Lake Rotorua. The perfect way to relax, recover, and complete a day of culture, adventure, and wellbeing.

What's included

Fully guided walking tour led by e

The ultimate – a 90 minute guided tour telling the story of the Northern Royal Albatross and the People history of Pukekura/Taiaroa Head.
Duration

1.5 Hours

About

This 90-minute fully-guided tour includes a short film, presentation on the albatross breeding cycle and a short walk up the hill for viewing from our exclusive glassed observatory to view the albatross and then continuing through the underground fort tunnels to see the fully restored Armstrong Disappearing Gun.

Learn about our exciting history. From a small Maori camp in the 1300s to a fortified Pa where the Treaty of Waitangi was signed in 1840; from a wooden flagstaff to an 1864 lighthouse at the entrance to Otago Harbour; from an 1880s underground fort to a large defence base in WWII. Taiaroa Head is today a Nature Reserve and iconic wildlife attraction.

tours.description:
Pōhatu is the largest Australasian Little Penguin colony on mainland New Zealand.

This is a wonderful option for people who wish to take part in our monitoring program and learn more, in-depth, about our conservation efforts. This gives you great insight into the life of a penguin and an opportunity to see the birds up close.

First, you will set off with a walk around the colony to monitor nesting sites and make sure that our little penguins are doing well. Then, you will have the opportunity to spot some undisturbed from our hides, socializing on the water with our binoculars and our telescope, and at dusk a likelihood of some returning to shore. We depart before it gets too dark and leave it for the penguins to do their thing without us in their way.

tours.description:
Discover the magnificent Okarito Lagoon
Duration

5 hours

About

Did you know?
Okarito lagoon is New Zealand’s largest unmodified wetland area - surrounded by national park and rainforest, home to a variety of wading and forest birds and takes a special place in the history books of the West Coast.

Join Paula & Swade onboard the 'Explorer Douglas'. During your 2 hour EcoTour they engage in both an informative and friendly way to help you discover the absolute magic of Okarito and its environment - from wetlands to rainforest and mountain landscapes, and an amazing diverse range of bird life.
Then our local guide will meet you off the boat at the wharf us for a 3 hour guided walk. With mountain and glacier views, flora & fauna, lagoon, beach, rich history, amazing sunrises & the best bird song in the area, this is one of New Zealand's hidden gems.

What to Bring

Outdoor clothing for the day’s weather conditions, spare warm top layer of clothing, comfortable walking shoes, sun hat, sunblock, lip balm, sunglasses, camera & water bottle.

2 hours guided tour on the “Explorer Douglas” - customised for the Okarito lagoon and wetlands

See rare yellow-eyed penguins, blue penguins and NZ fur seals in their breeding grounds on this 3.5hrs return tour of Natures Wonders on the Otago Peninsula.
Duration

3 Hours

About

The remote beaches at Natures Wonders are a breeding ground for remarkable wildlife. This coach tour takes you across farmland to wildlife viewing areas where you’ll see penguins, seals and cormorants in their natural habitat.
The scenery is incredible, but it’s the wildlife that steals the show on this fully-guided, small-group tour.
You’ll see:

Hoiho yellow-eyed penguins (one of the world’s rarest)
Blue penguins (the world’s smallest), and
NZ fur seals (one of the cutest).

Keep an eye skyward and you might catch a glimpse of the majestic Royal Albatross - the bird with the world’s largest wingspan.

The journey to Natures Wonders is as as the destination. The drive there takes you over the high road of the Otago Peninsula to Taiaroa Head. Along the way you’ll take in the spectacular views of remote beaches, steep rolling hills, rustic farmhouses and picturesque inlets. You will also stop (photo stop) for a look at Otakou Marae before continuing to your destination.

Witness the enchanting glowworms and spectacular limestone formations at Waitomo, then immerse yourself in the cultural and geothermal heart of Rotorua. Experience bubbling mud pools, erupting geysers, and steaming vents, showcasing nature’s raw power. Enjoy an authentic Māori cultural performance and a traditional Hangi buffet lunch, infused with indigenous flavors. This carefully curated experience offers a seamless blend of nature, culture, and adventure, ensuring a journey through New Zealand’s unique landscapes.

If paddleboarding isn't your thing and you feel more comfortable on a kayak, we have got you covered! Kayaks can fare a little better in windier conditions and you can paddle a bit further in a kayak than a SUP, so come and explore with us on the water!

Hire a single sit on top sea kayak and cruise the Haven at your leisure. Suitable for kids, right up to full-grown adult kids, we suggest children are accompanied with a strong paddler on each kayak.

Following a briefing on the conditions and any tips you need for your kayaking, you are free to enjoy the bay lapping up the sun or you can paddle out to Fifeshire Rock or Haulashore Island and enjoy the best that Tahunanui has to offer, from the water.

A 30 minute guided tour of underground Fort Taiaroa, built on the headland to counter the potential threat of a Russian invasion in the late 1880s and later used for training and defence during WWI and WWII. See the only fully restored 1889 Armstrong Disappearing Gun in the world in its original position.
Duration

30 minutes

About

Fort Taiaroa, established over 100 years ago to counter the threat of invasion from Tsarist Russia, is hidden beneath the albatross colony. Visitors can explore this fascinating secret fort, learn the military history, from Maori pa to WW2 Fort and view the only Armstrong Disappearing Gun of its type in the world, still in working trim, in its original gun pit. It’s a must-do tour to gain a full appreciation of this precious historic and wildlife site – you’ll be engrossed by the interesting stories of life during the military eras.

Things to Know

About

This tour is more than just visiting the filming sites! On this informative tour, your guide will share fascinating little-known gems relating to the filming at each site, that will make you want to watch the films all over again!

From your hotel or i-Site pickup we make our way to the Hutt Valley. The first stop is the Dry Creek Quarry where you see the filming site of Helm’s Deep and Minas Tirith.

A short drive will see us stop at the River Anduin (Hutt River) where the Fellowship travelled to Amon Hen.

Then it is on to the site of Gardens of Isengard (Harcourt Park) where Gandalf met Saruman the White to discuss the Ring, and it is also where Saruman’s Orc army destroy the gardens.

Take this fantastic opportunity to visit the Royal Albatross Centre at Taiaroa Head. This breath-taking location on the Otago Peninsula is home to the only mainland Northern Royal Albatross breeding colony in the world.

See it with Awesome Tours.

tours.description:
Get instant access to Nelson’s premium mountain bike trails with our Casual Shuttle Rides. Avoid the long uphill grinds and focus on the fun of descending single-track. Starting at the Codgers Mountain Bike Hub, our shuttle takes you to key trail drop-off points such as the Firball skid (250m vertical gain) or the top of Fringed Hill (650m vertical gain). From there, choose your own adventure—flowing intermediate runs, challenging technical descents, or advanced expert-only trails.

Our new online booking system ensures you can plan ahead, securing your seat and giving you peace of mind. For spontaneous riders, any unbooked seats remain available on a first-come, first-served basis on the day. Whether y
highlights:
Shuttle Transport:
Transporting riders and their bikes from the Codgers MTB Hub to designated trail access points.

Knowledgeable Driver:
A friendly, experienced driver familiar with local trails and conditions.

Flexible Booking Options:
Book online in advance for guaranteed seats or try your luck queuing up on the day.

Food and Drinks:
Pack your own water, snacks, or energy bars to stay fueled on the trails. Gravity's bike shop at 140 Bridge st, Nelson sells mountain biking nutrition products.

Arrival at Codgers MTB Hub (Before Your Slot):
Arrive at least 10 minutes before your booked departure time (or earlier if lining up for an unbooked seat).

Load Up and Departure (0 minutes):
Load your bike onto the shuttle trailer under staff guidance.

Scenic Drive (10-30 minutes):
Enjoy a short, scenic ride up the access roads as you gain vertical elevation the easy way.

Drop-Off at Selected Trailhead (~30 minutes):
Unload your bike at the top, where you’ll have direct access to a range of trails. Your adventure downhill begins here!

tours.name: Onedayer Adventure
tours.description:
(Minimum 2 pax for canoe part) The tour departs from Pipiriki with a 55 minute jet boat journey upriver 32 kms to the Mangapurua Landing, through an area of spectacular natural features with deep river gorges covered with green tree ferns and lush native vegetation. With your guide we will take you on an easy grade 40 minute walk from the Mangapurua landing following in the footsteps of the early pioneers along the old roadway to the “BRIDGE TO NOWHERE” where you will stop for lunch on this historical monument of a bygone era and learn the history from your local guide.​

The tour then includes Jet boat back down river 22kms and do an unguided 2 hours canoe or kayak (last 10 kms) back to Pipiriki stopping and exploring along the way.

What's included

Tea, coffee, hot chocolate and Biscuits
Canoe part: Canoes, Life jackets, Barrels and drybag

tours.description:
Kia ora Te Araroa Trail Hikers!

After weeks of trekking Aotearoa’s wild heart, it’s time to rest those legs and experience one of New Zealand’s Great Walks — by canoe!
Swap your hiking boots for a paddle and drift down the legendary Whanganui River on an 5-Day / 4-Night journey from Whakahoro to Whanganui.

🌊 Why Join This Adventure?

Rest & Recover: Let the current carry you while your legs enjoy a well-earned break.

Campsites: Sleep under star-filled skies beside the tranquil river at remote DOC and private sites.

Rich Culture & Nature: Paddle through lush bush, encounter native birds, and feel the living spirit of the Whanganui — an ancestral river steeped in Māori history.

🏕️ Journey Overview

Your scenic voyage begins at Whakahoro, winding through deep-green valleys and past iconic landmarks such as the Bridge to Nowhere — a powerful reminder of early settlers’ hopes and hardships.
Each paddle stroke takes you deeper into the serenity of Whanganui National Park, finishing in the riverside city of Whanganui.

tours.name: Climbing & Bouldering - The Jurassic Climbs
tours.description:
The Jurassic Climbs is the name of the bouldering and climbing crags at Waipu Caves Farm Park. The rock is hard limestone of good quality with fluted tops and flags on some edges.

THIS BOOKING IS FOR PEOPLE CLIMBING THEMSELVES WITH THEIR OWN EQUIPMENT. IT IS NOT A GUIDED OR SUPERVISED ACTIVITY.

There is about 75 routes spread across 3 crags 12m high and many boulders. With your own equipment you can top rope climb, lead climb, trad climb or boulder climb.

At The top of the crags there are hangers to use so you can easily access the pairs of hangers for top rope setup.

For trad climbing there are a few sections you could use your hardware.

Boulders have many boulders to pick from. You can hire mats at the office for $5 each per day.

The rock is kept clean so you can climb with maximum grip without the need for wire brushing moss or lichen.

The crags and boulders are spread around several spots and most are within 300m of the car park. With so many options we can handle about 60 climbers at a time.

You can see us listed on The Crag and Climb NZ under the name Waipu Caves Farm Park.

There is also a camp ground with toilets, hot showers, and fully equipped kitchen. There are snacks at the office.

If you are camping here you get free access to the climbing and bushwalking.

About

If paddleboarding isn't your thing and you feel more comfortable on a kayak, we have got you covered! Kayaks can fare a little better in windier conditions and you can paddle a bit further in a kayak than a SUP, so come and explore with us on the water!

Hire a single sit on top sea kayak and cruise the Haven at your leisure. Suitable for kids from approx 8yrs old, right up to full-grown adult kids, our kayaks are stable and fun!

Following a briefing on the conditions and any tips you need for your kayaking, you are free to enjoy the bay lapping up the sun or you can paddle out to Fifeshire Rock or Haulashore Island and enjoy the best that Tahunanui has to offer, from the water.

Top Tip: For the summer months, the wind tends to pick up throughout the day, so come earlier in the day for best conditions! If the wind is too strong to be safe on the ocean, we will contact you in advance to move your booking.

Please arrive 10 minutes early to kit up, sign in and be briefed.

Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or disrupt your visit.
Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But they will happen again.
DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.

tours.name: Māori Cultural Experience & Dinner Buffet
tours.description:
We bring you the ultimate cultural experience!

Enter the world of Mitai, and learn about the history of this area which was once flourished in villages.

Cultural Performance & Experience!

Our stories unfold through the dynamic scenes of warriors paddling the war canoe down Wai-o-Whiro stream. The melodious sounds of instruments and entertainment are highlighted through the haka and performing arts. Enjoy the traditional Hangi dinner followed by an evening walk through the forest visiting the old village site and discovering the sacred natural spring Te Puna Tapu a Tuhoe. End the evening in awe of the glow worms lighting the banks of the forest.

Buffet, the delicious tempting traditional hangi food of the Great Ocean of Kiwa!

Our hāngī earth oven kai (food) includes meat, chicken, kumara and much more.

The hāngī is cooked in an earth-oven, a hole 1-2m into the ground, the baskets of kai are placed on hot stones at the bottom of a hāngī pit. The kai is then covered to trap the heat, the steam and heat from heated hāngī stones infuses the kai with delicious earthy flavours while it cooks for 3-4 hours. Come and try out the delicious tempting food.

Experience two tours in one day, get a special deal when you book a full day trip!

After we Pick you up from Auckland CBD, We start our journey south of Auckland through a two and a half hours scenic drive into The Waikato Region towards Waitomo Glow Worm Caves.

Once we arrive, you will have a chance to get a snack or warm drink at the cafe. Then you’ll be escorted by The Waitomo Caves tour guide to start your tour inside Waitomo Grotto.

Inside the cave, you’ll be Walking through the marvelous natural light display created by the tiny living worms that are unique to New Zealand while listening to your tour guide explain the history and significance of the Grotto.

Then you’ll hop on board a flat bottom boat that will take you through the Waitomo River where you will get really close to the fascinating glowing creatures.

After that; you’ll Jump back on our luxurious vehicle to start our two-hour drive to Rotorua.

Tour Summary

Prepare for a day of wonder, fascination, and discovery as you immerse yourself in the unique environment of Waimangu Volcanic Valley on this luxurious private day tour from Auckland. Explore the world’s youngest geothermal valley on scenic walking trails surrounded by steaming landscapes, rare native birdlife, and vibrant volcanic features. Then cruise across Lake Rotomahana, the final resting place of the lost Pink and White Terraces—once known as the eighth wonder of the world. This journey blends geothermal beauty, natural history, and serene lake views in one extraordinary experience.

Escape the city and journey into the heart of New Zealand’s underground wonders on a premium private tour from Auckland to Waitomo. Marvel at the mesmerizing glow of the native Arachnocampa Luminosa as you glide silently through the world-famous Waitomo Glowworm Caves, then continue your adventure with a guided walking tour of Ruakuri Cave, where ancient limestone formations and hidden waterfalls create a spectacle. Enjoy seamless travel in a luxury private vehicle with a knowledgeable driver guide, and savor a relaxing café-style lunch before your return to Auckland, making this a full-day experience.

tours.name: Wildlife & Penguin Tour
tours.description:
Our 1.5 hour Wildlife & Penguin tour offers the most exclusive opportunity to view a variety of wildlife within our private eco-reserve. The reserve is home to New Zealand fur seals, sea lions, hoiho (yellow-eyed penguins), kororā (little penguins), forest birds, seabirds, and much more while contributing to conservation.
Your journey begins in a theatre setting, where you’ll learn about our dedicated conservation work to protect the critically endangered hoiho (Yellow-eyed Penguin), alongside efforts to restore the native flora and fauna. From there, a short bus ride takes you into the heart of the reserve, where you’ll embark on a guided nature walk of approximately 2 kilometres (1.25 miles). Along the way, you never know what you might see—each day offers a unique experience.

Hoiho are the rarest penguin species in the world, with fewer than 500 individuals remaining
on mainland New Zealand—and their population is continuing to decline. While sightings vary throughout the year, your tour includes a visit to our rehabilitation centre (when penguins are in care),
highlights: Fully guided tour with expert guide
Rain jackets provided
Binoculars available
Food and Drink
Learn about our conservation efforts and future plans
Explore a stunning nature reserve
Guided tour with expert knowledgeable staff
Contribute to conservation

tours.name: The Serenity River Expedition
tours.description:
🌊✨ Experience the Spirit of Aotearoa on a 4-Day Guided Journey on the Whanganui River! ✨🌊

Imagine gliding down the majestic Whanganui River, surrounded by landscapes and the rich tapestry of Māori culture. Join us for an 4-Day, 3-Night Guided and Catered River Journey, where you will be lead by local Kaitiaki (guides), the guardians of the land and river, who are tangata whenua (people of the land).

In a traditional waka (canoe), you will not only experience the serenity of the river but also connect deeply with the stories, traditions, and wisdom of the Māori people. Each paddle stroke will take you through lush native bush, past cliffs, and into the heart of a culture that has thrived for centuries.

🍃 What to Expect:

Culturally Enriching Experiences: Engage with local customs and stories that bring the landscape to life.
Scenery: Discover the natural beauty of Aotearoa, from tranquil waters to lush riverbanks.
Community Connection: Build lasting friendships with fellow adventurers and the Kaitiaki guidin
highlights: Free night accommodation at our Base in Owhango the night prior to your journey departure.
Rapid Water Flow: The Whanganui River features various sections with different water flow speeds. Sudden changes in flow can present challenges, especially for novice paddlers.
Obstacles: The river is home to natural obstacles such as fallen trees, rocks, and shallow areas. Navigating these hazards requires skill and awareness.
Weather Conditions: Weather can change rapidly in this region. Rain can lead to increased river flows and potential flooding. Always check the forecast before heading out.
Wildlife Encounters: While the river is home to beautiful wildlife, encounters with animals can pose risks. Be cautious and respectful of their habitats.
Hypothermia: Even in warmer months, the temperature of the water can be quite cold. Proper gear is essential to mitigate the risk of hypothermia.
Fatigue: Paddling can be physically demanding, especially on longer trips. It’s important to pace yourself and take regular breaks to avoid exhaustion.
Navigation Skills: Understanding how to read river maps and navigation skills are crucial. Being lost or disoriented can lead to dangerous situations.

tours.name: City to Sea Wildlife Cruise + Peninsula Bus Tour
tours.description:
Discover the wildest corners of Dunedin on land and sea!

Bus out from the city along the beautiful Otago Peninsula. Hear stories of sea creatures and early settlers as you pass quaint little townships and rolling farmland. You'll be presented with great views of the harbour and rugged coastline.

At Wellers Rock Wharf, you’ll board the Wildlife Cruise and travel out into the ocean, enjoying the scenery as we search for royal albatross, fur seals and other unique Southern Ocean creatures.

Your tour concludes with a relaxed cruise along the picturesque Otago Harbour, before returning you to Dunedin City.

What's included

Multi-language information sheets

Binoculars

Warm & waterproof jackets

Full commentary and assistance spotting wildlife

Fully licensed bar (snacks & beverages available to buy)

Tea & Coffee

Free wifi

Accommodation transfers (if required)

What's not included
We do not provide any sea sickness medication.
If you're worried, you can purchase it from local pharmacies. We do sell pressure point wristbands and people swear by them!

tours.name: Kaituna White Water Sledging | Rotorua
tours.description:
Kaitiaki Adventures are New Zealand’s original white water sledging specialists - since 1999

Dive into a one-of-a-kind adventure on the Kaituna River that combines thrilling rapids with the rich cultural significance of the area. This sledging experience lets you take on the river at eye level, navigating through native scenery, playholes, and exciting rapids. Unlike traditional rafting, you’re in control of your own vessel, using flippers to power your way through the water, with guidance and support from our expert team.

As you conquer the river, you'll also learn about the Kaituna’s deep connection to local Māori culture. The river is steeped in history, and our guides will share the stories of its significance, blending adventure with cultural appreciation. This experience offers awesome family fun, with a perfect mix of adrenaline and meaningful engagement with the land.

Confidence in treading water is necessary, but no prior experience

tours.name: 40 Minutes - Extended Whale Watching Flight
tours.description:
Take to the skies for a unique view on a whale-watching flight over Kaikoura. With a guaranteed window seat, all passengers get great views of the coastline and its marine life below.

Cover large ocean distances to maximize whale-watching opportunities by plane
Enjoy spectacular aerial views of sperm whales and dusky dolphins in Kaikoura
Take fantastic, unimpeded photos from your guaranteed window seat on the flight
Search for playful humpback whales, imposing orcas and mighty blue whales
Take in panoramic views of NZ alpine and coastal scenery from the air

An extended flight for the best chance of finding different species of marine life, with the focus on finding sperm whales. If time allows, we will have a look at the peninsula, the seal colony and the Kaikoura ranges.

What's included

40 Minute Flight

Window Seat

Live Commentary

Small Groups (maximum 7 passengers per aircraft)

Experienced nature guides (with a phone and first aid kit)

Torch

By the time you return to your ship you’ll understand why Dunedin is the Wildlife Capital of NZ!

About:

We’ll pick you up from the Port Chalmers Cruise Terminal and shuttle you 5-minutes to our boat, the Vivienne J. Once aboard the boat your expert crew will take you on a Wildlife Cruise around the Otago Harbour and beyond.

The small-group cruise will travel around beautiful wharves and boatsheds, then through the historic Quarantine Islands. You’ll see the Careys Bay fishing village and its motley collection of boats before continuing along the harbour. Enjoy a nice hot drink and biscuit for morning tea.

As you arrive at the entrance to the Otago Harbour you’ll see the tidal Aramoana sandflats and the spectacular volcanic cliffs of Taiaroa Head. You’ll see the royal albatross breeding colony, the only mainland colony in the world. Beneath a picturesque lighthouse you’ll find a large population of fur seals, watch as they swim, play and sleep on rocky platforms close to the boat. About

We’ll pick you up from the Port Chalmers Cruise Terminal. You’ll be greeted by one of our friendly staff holding a sign with your name printed clearly on it. From there you’ll bus along the western side of the Otago Harbour to Dunedin.

Your bus journey will take you up over the Otago Peninsula High Road to Larnach Castle. Along the way you’ll be treated to magnificent views of the rugged coastline and beautiful harbour.

Your guide will then take you on a personalised tour of Larnach Castle. Built in 1871, it took two hundred workers roughly three years to build the exterior shell and a further twelve years for master European craftsmen to finish the interior. Over the years the castle and grounds fell in to ruin and disrepair. In 1967 the property was bought by the Barker family who have spent many years restoring it to its former grandeur. The rooms are once again filled with original artworks, clothing and furniture.

tours.name: Hobbiton and Rotorua Tour
tours.description:
Make the best of your time in New Zealand and save money when you book two tours in one day with the Hobbiton and Te Puia Tour!

The tour starts with us picking you up from Auckland CBD, then, you will enjoy a two-hour scenic drive to Hobbiton through the Waikato Region.

At The Hobbiton Village, your guide will take on the Hobbiton bus to visit the Hobbit Holes, The Mill, The Double Arched Bridge, and have a complimentary drink at The Green Dragon Inn.

After you finish your guided 2.5-hour Hobbit trip, we start our way to Rotorua, where we visit Te Puia.

There, you’ll enjoy a day in a historic Maori Village to learn about the way they used to live and watch them carve and weave.

You’ll also see Mud Pools, the largest geyser in the Southern Hemisphere The Pohuto Geyser and watch our Native Kiwi Birds.

After approximately two hours, we head back to Auckland CBD.

What's included

Pick up from Auckland CBD.

Snacks & water

Stops for scenic Photo taking

Admission & 2.5-hour Guided tour in the Hobbiton Movie set

Free Beer, Ginger Beer, or Cider at Green Dragon Inn.

1hr drive to Rotorua

tours.name: Wairoa River Rafting
tours.location: New Zealand/Bay of Plenty Region/Okere Falls
tours.description:
The Wild Wairoa River!!

This wild river is renowned for having some of the best white water action here in New Zealand.

A level up from the Kaituna this trip is not for the faint of heart, for this trip you need to have strong swimming skills and be up for an adventure!

Kaituna Cascades run the whole of the river including the bottom three rapids and the lower waterfall!
Hold on for dear life as you tackle ‘Mother's Nightmare’ which has a technical grade 4 rock garden, closely followed by a tight 2 metre drop!!

Experience the thrill of ‘The Rollercoaster’ – consisting of the aptly named ‘Devils Cauldron’ and the ‘Bottom Drop’. Feel the rush of ‘The Waterfall’ which has an awesome 3 metre drop into a churning pool of white water through the Wairoa Rivers boulder-strewn rock canyon.

Minimum Numbers

tours.name: Hobbiton Private Transfer Tour
tours.description:
Visitors have the opportunity to tour the famous filming location utilized by Peter Jackson for his well-known Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit movie trilogies on the Hobbiton Movie Set Tour.

The Hobbiton Movie Set has been one of New Zealand's most popular tourist destinations for the past ten years.

The tour begins with a pick-up service from Auckland's central business district and includes private transportation. Visitors will take pleasure in a two-hour scenic trip into Waikato, with opportunities for photo stops along the way and other essential pauses.

Visitors are given 30 to 45 minutes after arrival to browse the authorized Hobbiton Gift Shop and enjoy a meal at the renowned Shire's Rest Cafe.

Guests then board The Hobbiton Bus, which will take them to The Hobbit Village, and the Middle-earth adventure officially starts. An in-depth two-and-a-half-hour group tour of this location is given by an expert who covers The Hobbit Holes, The Mill, The Double Arched Bridge, and includes a free drink at The Green Dragon Inn.

Expect to take countless pictures and vid

tours.name: Auckland Maori Experience Private Tour
tours.description:
Become part of our whanau (Family) and learn about New Zealand’s beautiful Maori culture through this amazing experience.

Watch Haka Performance (War Dance) directly from knowledgeable and passionate descendants of the land wearing traditional clothes.

Explore rare and spectacular plants in an ever-changing display that can be seen in each of the two barrel-vaulted Victorian-style glass houses in the Winter Gardens. Your tour guide will teach you about our Authentic Musical Instruments, Dances, and Games that our ancestors have used for generations.

Enjoy a delicious Lunch and learn about the culture of sharing Kai (food).

To enhance your experience, we offer two exciting optional add-ons (additional charges apply). You can choose one or enjoy both for a deeper, more immersive journey:

Private Poi-Making Hands-On Experience: Discover the art and cultural significance of traditional Māori poi through a guided interactive workshop.

Private Māori Portrait Guided Tour at Auckland Art Gallery: Explore powerful Māori portraiture with an expert guide and gain deeper insight into the stories behind the artworks.

Enjoy the scenery while we cross the Iconic Harbour Bridge that connects Auckland city to the suburb of North Shore while you learn about the history of the location.

Climb the summit of Mount Victoria, where you’ll discover Devonport’s Disappearing Gun, one of only a few left in the world.

tours.name: Waitomo Gloworm Cave + Te Puia Geothermal Valley Private Tour

Embark on an exclusive guided combo private tour, immersing yourself in the wonders of both the Waitomo Glow Worm Caves and Te Whakarewarewa Geothermal Valley, all in one day. Begin your adventure by delving into the mystical depths of the Waitomo Glowworm Caves, where you'll encounter the unique Arachnocampa luminosa species, casting an ethereal glow throughout the caverns.

Then, journey to the captivating Te Whakarewarewa Geothermal Valley, where you'll marvel at Rotorua's famed mud pools and the awe-inspiring Pohutu Geyser, the largest active geyser in the Southern Hemisphere. As you explore, don't miss the chance to encounter live Kiwi Birds and observe skilled artisans at work, showcasing traditional Māori carving and weaving techniques.

Immerse yourself further in Māori culture with captivating Cultural Performances, featuring traditional storytelling, music, and dance. With this guided combo tour, you'll optimize your exploration of New Zealand's natural wonders and rich cultural heritage, creating memories to last a lifetime.

Muriwai Beach is one of the most famous black sand beaches in New Zealand, known for surfing and home to the beautiful seabirds “Gannets”.

With different lookouts surrounding the area, you will have a close encounter with the gannets at Muriwai Gannet Colony and on Motutara Island (Gannets season is from August until March every year).

We will then head to the beautiful Tamaki Drive along the eastern coast of Auckland City all the way up to Bastion Point, known as Michael Savage Memorial, discovering some of the City’s highlights, including Achilles Point.

Before heading back, we will visit The Historical Victorian Style Domain Winter Gardens, which are a complex of gardens located within the Auckland Domain.

tours.name: Māori Rock Carvings - Luxury Sailing Catamaran Tiua - 3.30pm
tours.description:
Step aboard Tiua, Taupō Sailing Adventures’ luxurious sailing catamaran, for a relaxing and scenic afternoon on the water. As the lake settles into the warmth of the day, enjoy a smooth and peaceful cruise toward the iconic Māori Rock Carvings—an awe-inspiring 14-metre artwork carved into the cliffs and only accessible by boat.

This eco-friendly sailing experience is powered by the wind, offering a quiet and gentle way to connect with the natural beauty of Lake Taupō. With her stable twin-hull design, Tiua provides a smooth ride and plenty of space to stretch out and enjoy the journey. Her spacious saloon, covered cockpit, and open deck areas are designed to keep you comfortable in all weather.

While sailing, enjoy a complimentary beer, wine, or non-alcoholic beverage as you take in the spectacular views.

tours.name: Rangitaiki River Rafting
tours.location: New Zealand/Bay of Plenty Region/Okere Falls
tours.description:
The Rangitaiki is an awesome half day Wilderness rafting trip passing through spectacular NZ scenery and Native bush.

Kaituna Cascades normally offers the Rangitaiki River Rafting Tours while the Kaituna river is flooded. Generally it’s low rocky and bouncy, but after the rains that close & flood the Kaituna river – the “Rangi” becomes and class 4/5 beast and a brown rollercoaster of fun!

The Rangitaiki is an awesome half day Wilderness rafting trip passing through spectacular NZ scenery and Native bush between the Kaiangaroa forest and the beautiful and untouched Te Urewera National Park.

The Rangi is the complete rafting package with continuous and hard whitewater at the start of the river, with larger rapids like Geoff’s Joy, Fantail Falls, Pop Up, and Tautika getting ya pumped up and holding on tight…

Then chilling out in the middle with a nice quiet flat stretch, ideal for swimming and floating followed by fun grade 3+ rapids through to the finish.

Once you’ve rafted the epic 12 km’s!! of whitewater – we’ll cruise back to Rotorua!

tours.name: Hobbiton Movie Set Tour
tours.description:
Experience the film set of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings fame!

The Hobbiton Movie Set Tour is where Peter Jackson filmed his famous Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit film trilogies.

The Hobbiton Movie Set is one of the most visited destinations in New Zealand for the past 10 years.

Tour starts by picking you up from Auckland CBD, then you’ll enjoy a two-hour scenic drive South of Auckland into Waikato, with a scenic stop for amazing photos and any other stops if needed.

Once we arrive, you spend 30–45 mins shopping in the official Hobbiton Gift Shop and grabbing a drink or a bite in the famous Shire’s Rest Café.

Then your middle earth Journey starts by hopping on The Hobbiton Bus that takes you to The Hobbit Village where your guide will do a two-hour guided tour through The Hobbit Holes, The Mill, The Double Arched Bridge and have a complimentary drink at The Green Dragon Inn.

Be prepared to take lots of photos and videos in this unique place.

After you finish your amazing Hobbit tour, we make our way through the scenic roads of Waikato back to Auckland CBD.

tours.name: Waitomo Glowworm Cave Tour
tours.description:
Enjoy the Waitomo Glowworm Cave Tour with Auckland & Beyond Tours. New Zealand has a unique species of tiny glowing creatures called “Arachnocampa Luminoso.” Thousands of these magical tiny living lights radiate their luminescent light all around the Waitomo Grotto. The tour starts by picking you up from Auckland CBD. Then, we go on a two-and-a-half-hour scenic drive in South Auckland and into the Waikato region, with a scenic stop for amazing photos and any other stops if needed. On arrival, you will have around 30 minutes for some shopping in the Gift Shop and grabbing a drink or something to eat at the Waitomo Homestead. Your Guide will take you on a 45-minute tour inside the Waitomo Glowworm Cave, explaining the history of the Cave, the glowing worms, and the formations you’ll see inside. Afterward, you’ll ride on a flat-bottom boat that will glide through the Waitomo river while you gaze silently at the sparkling worms. After you finish your Glowworm Experience, we will make our way back through the scenic roads to Auckland CBD.

tours.name: Bay of Islands Tour
tours.description:
This Full-day tour in search of Dolphins and other Marine life in New Zealand is definitely a must do while visiting Bay of Island.

Tour starts with us picking you up from Auckland CBD, then we head north of Auckland on a three-hour scenic drive into The Far North District.

When you arrive in Paihia you will go to the Wharf to start your 4-hours guided boat cruise.

You will be cruising on the Catamaran Dolphin seeker around the islands searching for dolphins and other marine life. You will have a stopover in Urupukapuka Island where you can just relax on the beach or walk to the top of the island to enjoy 360° views of this beautiful region. You will be visiting the famous Hole in the Rock on Motukokako Island, as the boat sails right to the end of the Cape Brett Peninsula.

Then we head back to Auckland CBD through the scenic roads of the Northland.

tours.description:
The Coromandel Day Tour starts with us picking you up from Auckland CBD; then you’ll enjoy a Two and half-hour drive through the Waikato Region then Bay Of Plenty with a scenic stop on the way for amazing photos and any other stops if needed. Then we head down to Visit the Driving Creek Railway that will take you on a 1-hour train ride that includes 2 spirals, 3 short tunnels, 5 reversing points and several large viaducts as it climbs up the hill to the Eyefull Tower. At the top, you will be fascinated by the panoramic views over the island-studded Hauraki Gulf. After that; you will go to the White Sandy Coromandel Beach where you can enjoy a walk, Swim, or just Relaxing. Then you will visit the Coastal Walkway Cathedral Cove and the natural Thermal Mineral Pools of The Hot Water Beach. After you finish your amazing tour in The Coromandel Peninsula we start our way back to Auckland CBD. We customize tours to suit your requirements, just let us know when you make your booking and we will do our best to accommodate your request.

tours.name: West Coast Discovery Tour
tours.description:
Piha is New Zealand’s most famous surf beach, situated on the west coast of the North Island. This black iron-sand beach has a reputation for awesome surfs that roll in over the Tasman Sea. See this and more on our West Coast Discovery!

The tour starts with picking you up from Auckland CBD; then, you’ll enjoy a 30-minute scenic drive through the Waitakere Ranges. The first stop is the Arataki Visitor Centre, where you will learn all about New Zealand’s Native trees and look out to panoramic views of the Waitakere Ranges – the perfect start to exploring the west coast. We then take a 20-minute drive to Kitekite waterfalls.

Once we arrive at Kitekite waterfalls, you will enjoy a 5-minute easy stroll to the waterfall- a great spot for photos! We then head to the famous Piha Surf Beach, where you can go for a swim or just relax and enjoy the views.

You can also walk up the Lion Rock (situated in the middle of the beach) for views and an amazing photo opportunity. ​

After that, we head back to Auckland CBD.

tours.name: Discover Auckland City
tours.description:
We start by picking you up from Auckland CBD, then we head to Mission Bay waterfront suburb about 5 km east of Auckland CBD. Driving through the scenic Tamaki Drive with unobstructed views of Rangitoto Island

After that, we take you to MJ Savage Memorial Park, known as Bastion Point. Which overlooks the Harbour Bridge, Waitemata Harbour, and Auckland City Skyline.

We will also take you to Achilles Point, where you will capture some amazing photos with Rangitoto Island as your background; Rangitoto Island is the most recent and the largest Volcano in the Hauraki Gulf area.

One Tree Hill “Maungakiekie” is another volcanic summit in Auckland City, sets at 182-metre (597 ft) & the second-largest volcanic field intact in Auckland City. You will enjoy the 360 view of Auckland at One Tree hill summit and learn about the history of the mount.

Our Next Stop will be at Mount Eden Summit. One of the most prominent volcanic cones remaining in the Auckland region, where you’ll be able to see amazing views over the Hauraki Gulf.

Now our tour comes to an end, We drive back to Auckland CBD for your hotel drop off.

tours.name: Te Puia Geothermal Valley Rotorua
tours.description:
Visit one of New Zealand’s Geothermal wonders situated in the Whakarewarewa on a half day tour from Auckland City. Te Puia Geothermal Valley Rotorua is an active geothermal wonderland!

This 60-hectare site is home to the New Zealand Maori Arts and Crafts Institute, alive kiwi enclosure, the world-famous Pohutu Geyser, and more than 500 natural geothermal wonders.

Tour starts with us picking you up from Auckland CBD; then you enjoy a three-hour scenic drive towards the Bay of Plenty.

On arrival, you will be welcomed by the Māori residents and offered to choose your steam box meal (extra cost) to be cooked in Woven baskets and placed in the active steam vent.

After that; your tour guide will take you through a 60 mins tour around 60 hectares of Te Puia Geothermal Valley including the largest active geyser in the Southern Hemisphere, the Pohutu Geyser.

You can also See the native Kiwi bird, Mud Pools, watch New Zealand’s iconic native Carvings and Weaving performed in front of you, as well as Learning about the Māori Culture while performing at the sacred Marae.

tours.name: Rameka Track Shuttle
tours.description:
Nelson to Takaka

A great day exploring Golden Bay

Shuttle to ride the Rameka Tracks
Duration

Full day tour

About

Early morning shuttle (with coffee stop) to the top of Takaka hill. Ride the rugged & ramblinbg Rameka tracks down to Takaka. Return shuttle to Nelson.

If time allows, we can stop to complete a lap or two of the Pikikirunga track or Kaiteriteri MTB Park

*The Rameka track is a Grade 3+ trail, with some rough and technical sections. You will need to guide yourselves (TrailForks app recommended) and carry sufficient gear, spares, tools and first aid. There is limited phone reception, but the landscape and trails are a treat.

Track information: https://www.mtbtrailstrust.org.nz/rameka-track

tours.name: Great Taste Beer Tour (Circuit & City)
tours.description:
Ages 18+ • 6.5h • 30km off-road cycling, collection from town/accommodation, bike & beer tasting

This is an extended beer tour option where we will highlight the many thirst-quenching bars and breweries including two awesome beer tasting experiences
Duration

Approx. 10:30am-5pm

About

Visit some of Nelson's best breweries and watering holes whilst cycling this cruisy circuit

The tour begins with a flat, off-road circuit to our favourite breweries on the outskirts of Nelson. You'll see working breweries whilst enjoying a beer tasting paddle at one of our favourite breweries / hop creationists.

You'll then head along along the cycle trail to Nelson where there are many more breweries and bars to choose from. The tour experience ends at an iconic Pub / nano brewery for a second complimentary beer tasting. This legendary Kiwi brew pub boasts an ever changing and extensive beer list from around the country

We'll collect the bikes and drop you home… or choose to stay in town to enjoy more fun and tasty treats!

Visit some of Nelson's best breweries, pubs and bars whilst cycling this cruisy, flat circuit.

You will enjoy coastal views and follow a short rail trail whilst cycling between a coastal country pub, historic tap room & breweries with hop-tastic delights.

Suitable for couples, families and groups of friends, there are many tasty options along the way.

Cover wide ocean areas to increase your chances of spotting sperm whales and dusky dolphins
Marvel at aerial views of Kaikoura’s unique peninsula, seal colony, and surrounding waters
Scan the sea for majestic blue whales, orcas, and playful humpbacks during their seasonal visits
Soar past the rugged Kaikoura Ranges, often blanketed in snow during winter months
Capture incredible photos of both marine life and alpine scenery from your guaranteed window seat

This extended flight offers the best chance of seeing multiple species of marine life while also showcasing the full beauty of Kaikoura’s coastline and mountains - a perfect combination of wildlife and wilderness from the air.

Woohoo - Come and have some fun on the BIG Tahuna! Bring your friends, family, colleagues or school friends for a real giggle on the water.

This is a great option for birthdays, parties, schools or businesses that want a real hoot, fun and games in our beautiful bay. Learn how to paddle in unison, use a board for some balancing challenges, wipe outs or a floating platform in the sunshine.

Suitable for all ages, the Big Tahuna is suitable for up to 10 children (intermediate/junior) or six to eight high school aged kids or adults.

We ask that you are comfortable in the water before hiring from us, and all equipment that you need for a great time is provided.

Please arrive 10 minutes early to kit up, sign in and be briefed.

Top Tip: For the summer months, the wind tends to pick up throughout the day, so come earlier in the day for best conditions! If the wind is too strong to be safe on the ocean, we will contact you in advance to move your booking.

​Experience the Best of Cape Kidnappers!
Duration

3 Days & 2 Nights

Tour Summary

Set off from Auckland on a 3-day luxury private tour through New Zealand’s North Island, beginning with the vibrant geothermal pools of Wai-O-Tapu and the powerful Huka Falls. Continue to Napier, renowned for its striking 1930s Art Deco architecture and coastal elegance. Explore Cape Kidnappers on a 4WD safari to one of the world’s largest mainland gannet colonies, perched above dramatic ocean cliffs. On your return journey, unwind with a scenic Lake Taupō cruise to the iconic Māori Rock Carvings. With curated experiences, a private driver-guide, and 4-star accommodation, this journey offers the perfect blend of nature, culture, and comfort.

​Itinerary At a Glance

Day 1: Discover Wai-O-Tapu Thermal Wonderland, Huka falls and Travel to Napier. Overnight Stay in Napier.

Day 2: Cape Kidnappers Gannet Safari Tour & Art Deco Walking City Tour. Overnight Stay in Napier.

Day 3: Lake Taupo Waterfront, Māori Rock Carvin

Combine some of Marlborough's classic activities on this full-day tour: cruising on Queen Charlotte Sound to Ships Cove, enjoy a winery lunch and tasting some of the area's world-renowned wines.

Spend the morning out cruising aboard a Beachcomber Cruises catamaran on a scenic cruise to Ships Cove, then return to Picton and be transferred down to the wine region for a lunch and wine tasting at one of Marlborough's famous Cellar Doors.

Embark on a private day tour from Auckland to explore the cultural and geothermal marvels of Rotorua. Dive into the heart of Māori traditions with an authentic hangi feast, mesmerizing cultural performances, and an exhilarating warrior canoe experience. The journey continues as you wander through the otherworldly landscapes of Wai-O-Tapu Thermal Wonderland, where bubbling hot springs, vibrant geothermal pools, and steaming geysers create a surreal and enchanting atmosphere.

tours.name: Hike and Kayak Combo
tours.description:
Looking for an active day? Join us for a full day of adventure combining a morning hike through endemic ancient forest down our private walking track to Pohatu bay and join our sea-kayaking safari in the afternoon to encounter Pohatu marine reserve wildlife.

After being picked up in Akaroa by our booking office you will be transported by 4WD mini-van to the beginning of a 3 hours hiking trail (regular to relaxed pace). With a map and instructions from your guide you will, at your leisure, walk down part of the famous Banks Track through ancient red beech tree forest and tree ferns to Pohatu bay.

Along the way discover many waterfalls and listen to native bird songs and visit the prehistoric forest of Tutakakahikura scenic reserve with trees over 400 years old.

Once arrived at Pohatu bay you will have access to a fully equipped kitchen and bathroom facilities to relax, eat and get ready for the afternoon sea-kayaking safaris starting at 12.45pm.

What's included

Scenic drive by 4WD mini vans
highlights: Scenic drive by 4WD mini vans
Self-guided hike through an ancient forest. A guided option can be arranged at extra cost
Access to a fully equipped communal area for lunch
Kayaking is fully guided by qualified guides
All gear for the sea-kayaking part of the activity (lifejackets, dry jackets, spray deck, dry bags for cameras…)
100% guarantee to see New Zealand Fur seal
Hiking boots or hiking shoes.
Sunglasses, hat or both

tours.name: Sea-kayaking Banks Track
tours.description:
Explore the outer coast of Pōhatu Marine Reserve by kayak and marvel at its spectacular towering cliffs, rock stacks, reefs, and deep-sea caves.

Flea Bay Island and the impressive island arch make an added exciting attraction in settled sea conditions. Observe the diverse wildlife and marine species such as penguins, seals, various sea birds and possibly the world’s smallest dolphin!

Best of all, no kayaking experience necessary! Trips are only run in settled, safe conditions by experienced and knowledgeable guides. Your safety is our top priority.

What's included

Fully guided by qualified and experienced staff
All kayaking gear (life jackets, dry jackets, spray deck, dry bags for cameras)
highlights: Wear something comfortable: leggings or board shorts - jeans are not suitable - or something you can roll up for when we get in and out of the kayak.

Wear layers that you can add/remove if it is too hot or cold.
You might also bring a spare change of clothes and a towel just in case you get wet.
A pair of shoes that you won’t mind getting wet while walking on rocks, on the beach and stepping in and out of the kayaks.
A bottle of water
Sun protection: hat, sunglasses, sunscreen
Option 1: No further tours. Full Refund.

Departing from the Kaikoura airport you will fly past the back of Mount Fyffe, over Lake Hapuku and then descend along the northern coastline. Your pilot will then fly you around the Kaikoura peninsula before returning to the airport.

Enjoy a panoramic scenic flight, with scenic views of the Seaward Kaikoura ranges and a birds eye view of the Kaikoura Peninsula. tours.name: Sheep & Beef Working Farm Private Tour
tours.description:
Discover What Makes New Zealand Sheep & Beef Farming Special.

Our Farm Tour includes a visit to a family-run sheep and beef farm where you will enjoy a guided tour of the property, interact with animals, and learn about traditional farming practices in New Zealand.

Your visit includes lunch served in a rural setting, offering a relaxing opportunity to take in the peaceful farm surroundings.

You will watch a live Sheep Shearing demonstration and witness the impressive skill of Sheep Dogs herding livestock across the paddocks – a true highlight of the Kiwi farming lifestyle.

This unique Farm Tour is exclusive to Auckland & Beyond Tours and offers a genuine glimpse into rural New Zealand.

• Pick up & drop off at any hotel, airport, or cruise port in Auckland.
